audience.description: Adults who post short videos every week for their own side project or small business: a baker, a freelance trainer, a shop owner, a hobby creator. They have a camera roll full of clips and little time. They want their posts to look finished and consistent without spending a whole evening editing.

brief.productRole: The phone stands upright on a desk. A finger taps a handful of clips from the camera roll and picks a length. The timeline of colored clip blocks snaps into a tight sequence, the preview plays with cuts landing on the beat, then a thumb nudges one clip and trims it before tapping post. The app edits the person's own footage, and the ad shows the messy roll turning into a finished short.

music.style: Upbeat modern indie pop with a clean finger-snap and clap groove, warm bass, light synth plucks, and a small drum fill on the final cut

visual.look: Bright natural daylight grade with soft warm highlights and gentle contrast, handheld-feeling but stable. Shot on a clean mid-wide lens with tight inserts on the phone screen. Fast pacing: cuts land on the beat every 1 to 1.5 seconds, a split of chaotic camera-roll scroll into a clean timeline, ending on a held shot of the sage green phone with the icon visible. Vertical framing with the subject in the upper two thirds so captions stay clear.

wardrobe.styling: Everyday working clothes: a flour-dusted apron over a plain tee, a soft knit sweater, a plain denim jacket, a canvas work shirt. Solid muted colors, no logos, no printed text.

types: cluttered creator desk by a window

voice.tone: Warm, direct, practical, a little playful
use: Names the real problem of footage piling up
Says what the app does: cuts, captions and pacing done for you
Mentions that you pick the clips and fine-tune before posting
Ends with a simple invitation to try it
avoid: Claims it generates people or writes ads
Speaking as a customer who tried it

hooks: Forty clips. One hour. Zero edits done.
Your camera roll is not a video yet.
Stop saving clips you never post.

talent.description: One fictional adult small-business owner, in a bakery kitchen, with flour on their hands, glancing at a phone. Then a second fictional adult creator at a desk scrolling a crowded camera roll. Both look relaxed and capable, with natural expressions, mid-twenties to early thirties in feel.
